I also need to be careful about floating-point contraction (FMA) settings under -O3, since that could affect bitwise equivalence between the two loop orderings.\n\nI'm also considering cache blocking/tiling over k, confirming that as long as k-blocks are processed in ascending order, the accumulation order per element is preserved. Since OpenMP or other threading would add dependencies beyond the MPI-only scope, I'll stick to MPI-based parallelism for distributing work across ranks while keeping the per-rank computation cache-blocked for performance.\n\nFor timing, I'll measure only the distributed multiply section using MPI_Barrier before and MPI_Reduce with MAX at the end to get worst-case elapsed time across ranks, keeping the same output format and Gflops formula as the original. For output and validation, I need to gather the distributed C matrix back to rank 0 using MPI_Gatherv with row blocks in rank order, which naturally reconstructs the original row-major layout for both full printing and checkpoint-based validation against expected values from A and B.\n\nActually, keeping full A on rank 0 just for validation seems wasteful at scale, especially since validation only really needs a handful of checkpoint rows, which may or may not fall on rank 0 depending on row distribution. I'm leaning toward reworking validateResult to accept an accessor function or sample specific elements on demand rather than requiring full local A.\n\nSince A(i,j) is just getPseudoRndValue(N,i,j), validation can recompute A and B values directly instead of storing them, which sidesteps the gathering problem entirely. For C, I'll gather the full matrix to rank 0 when printing is requested (-r), and for validation-only runs, just have the rank owning the sampled rows compute locally.\n\nFor argument parsing errors, since every rank gets identical argv, all ranks will detect the same invalid option simultaneously — so I just need rank 0 to print the error and then all ranks call MPI_Finalize before exiting, keeping things consistent.\n\nFor edge cases like N=0 or negative N, I'll preserve the original program's behavior rather than add extra validation, though I should make sure row distribution logic doesn't crash when rows-per-rank computes to zero. For splitting rows across ranks, I'm using a block distribution: base rows = N/P with remainder r = N%P assigned to the first r ranks, then using MPI_Gatherv with counts expressed in elements (rows*N) and corresponding displacements to reassemble the result matrix.\n\nFor timing, I'll synchronize all ranks with a barrier before starting the clock, measure elapsed time per rank, then reduce the max elapsed time across ranks to get the true parallel runtime, converting that into milliseconds the same way the original used duration_cast. For GFLOPS, I'm deciding to use the precise double-precision elapsed seconds rather than truncating to integer milliseconds first, since that gives a more accurate flop-rate calculation while still printing milliseconds in the same format as before.\n\nFor the actual matrix multiply kernel, each rank computes its local block of rows using a blocked i-k-j loop order with tiling over k and j, preserving the same ascending-k accumulation order as the original so the floating-point summation stays numerically equivalent, including matching behavior under fused multiply-add optimization.\n\nI'm picking block sizes (jb=256, kb=64) to keep working sets cache-resident, and noting that B is small enough to be recomputed redundantly on each rank rather than communicated, since that recomputation cost is negligible compared to the overall multiply.\n\nI'll keep the pseudo-random generator formula identical to the original to avoid overflow or correctness mismatches, since replicating B locally per rank is the simplest 1D approach versus more scalable but complex 2D schemes like SUMMA.\n\nFor output, I'm gathering the full C matrix on rank 0 via MPI_Gatherv only when printing or validating results, outside the timed region. Since this means O(N^2) memory on root, I'm considering whether validation really needs the full matrix or just the handful of sampled checkpoint rows, which would be cheaper but adds complexity — full gather is simpler and acceptable for now.\n\nI'm also reworking validateResult to accept the full gathered C and recompute A and B on the fly via getPseudoRndValue rather than passing around the distributed A/B arrays, since root doesn't have those locally — this changes the function signature but keeps the printed output identical. Finally, I'm updating the CMake setup to use find_package(MPI REQUIRED) and link against MPI::MPI_CXX, keeping the math library linked, and confirming this works even with a plain compiler as long as MPI is located.\n\nWriting the row partition logic...\n\nWriting cache-blocked multiply loop...\n\nStill writing blocked matmul loop...\n\nChecking that this tiled accumulation matches the original summation order, since c[j] initializes to zero and accumulates the same products as before.\n\nI'm also reasoning through cache blocking: the B block (64×256 doubles, ~128KB) gets reused across all i iterations, fitting L2 nicely, while the C row segment stays small enough for L1 reuse across k. Now I'm writing a validation function to check the result correctness.\n\nSetting up MPI init and rank/size...\n\nStill writing argument parsing and setup...\n\nI'm reducing the max local time across ranks to get the overall runtime, using MPI_Reduce with MAX after computing each rank's elapsed duration. I'm also noting that using MPI_Wtime would be a more standard way to measure timing in MPI programs compared to the clock library.\n\nNow I'm computing throughput in GFLOPs from the elapsed time and matrix size, and setting up the gather logic for collecting results across ranks when printing or validating output, building per-rank counts and displacements for an MPI_Gatherv call.\n\nI realize using plain int counts for MPI_Gatherv could overflow for extremely large N since N*N exceeds the 32-bit int range past roughly N=46340 — worth noting as a limitation for very large benchmark sizes, though the default N=512 is far from this threshold.\n\nI'm defining an MPI derived datatype representing one row of N doubles, so gather counts become expressed in rows rather than raw elements, avoiding the overflow issue while keeping the gather collective across all ranks regardless of whether a rank is root. I keep the print and validation logic ordered as in the original: print timing, then results, then validate on the root rank only.\n\nFor exit codes, I realize only rank 0 computes validity, so I should broadcast that result so every rank returns a consistent exit status rather than relying on mpirun's ambiguous handling of mixed return codes. I'm leaving the potential division-by-zero when N=0 and validation is requested as-is, since the original code has the same undefined behavior—not worth guarding against since it matches existing semantics.\n\nI'm checking edge cases: ranks with zero rows handle empty vectors fine since loops simply don't execute and nullptr buffers are safely ignored in MPI_Gatherv calls, and non-root buffers aren't touched in the gather operation.\n\nNow I'm writing the CMakeLists.txt file, setting the C++ standard to 20, finding the MPI package, and linking the matmul executable against MPI and math libraries.\n\nI'll leave the default project languages (C and CXX) unchanged since FindMPI works fine with that, and the -march=native and -O3 flags should work properly with the mpicxx wrapper. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793033985818,"sessionID":"ses_e86d9c73dffeXEMyYZnYJcH9C9","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01Ms4mh7Nf8SK38YH73PGTYT","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/matmul/matmul.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Generate pseudo-random values for matrix initialization\nconstexpr double getPseudoRndValue(const size_t N, const size_t i, const size_t j) noexcept {\n    return (((i + 1) * (i + j + 1) * 1299709) % (N * N)) / static_cast<double>(N * N);\n}\n\n// Row-block distribution of N rows across `size` ranks. The first (N % size)\n// ranks receive one extra row.\nstruct RowPartition {\n    size_t firstRow;\n    size_t numRows;\n};\n\nRowPartition partitionRows(const size_t N, const int rank, const int size) {\n    const size_t p = static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rank);\n    const size_t base = N / p;\n    const size_t extra = N % p;\n    return {r * base + std::min(r, extra), base + (r < extra ? 1 : 0)};\n}\n\n// Fill `numRows` rows of a row-major matrix, starting at global row `firstRow`.\n// `mat` must hold numRows * N elements.\nvoid initMatrixRows(std::vector<double>& mat, const size_t N, const size_t firstRow, const size_t numRows) {\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numRows; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            mat[i * N + j] = getPseudoRndValue(N, firstRow + i, j);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Local block multiply: C (numRows x N) = A (numRows x N) * B (N x N).\n// Cache-blocked i-k-j loop order with a contiguous, vectorizable inner loop.\n// For every C(i,j) the products are accumulated in ascending k order starting\n// from 0.0, which is the same summation order as the naive triple loop.\nvoid matrixMultiplyRows(const double* A, const double* B, double* C, const size_t numRows, const size_t N) {\n    constexpr size_t KB = 64;   // k-block: B panel of KB x JB doubles stays in L2\n    constexpr size_t JB = 256;  // j-block: C row segment stays in L1\n\n    std::fill(C, C + numRows * N, 0.0);\n\n    for (size_t jj = 0; jj < N; jj += JB) {\n        const size_t jEnd = std::min(jj + JB, N);\n        for (size_t kk = 0; kk < N; kk += KB) {\n            const size_t kEnd = std::min(kk + KB, N);\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < numRows; ++i) {\n                double* c = C + i * N;\n                const double* a = A + i * N;\n                for (size_t k = kk; k < kEnd; ++k) {\n                    const double aik = a[k];\n                    const double* b = B + k * N;\n                    for (size_t j = jj; j < jEnd; ++j) {\n                        c[j] += aik * b[j];\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Simple validation: compute a few elements of C from the generator and compare.\n// A(i,k) and B(k,j) are pure functions of their indices, so they are regenerated\n// here rather than requiring the full A and B on the validating rank.\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& C, const size_t N) {\n    // Check a few random positions\n    constexpr size_t checkPoints[] = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4};\n\n    for (size_t pi = 0; pi < 5; ++pi) {\n        for (size_t pj = 0; pj < 5; ++pj) {\n            const size_t i = checkPoints[pi] % N;\n            const size_t j = checkPoints[pj] % N;\n\n            double expected = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                expected += getPseudoRndValue(N, i, k) * getPseudoRndValue(N, k, j);\n            }\n\n            const double actual = C[i * N + j];\n            const double relError = std::abs((actual - expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n\n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at (%zu, %zu): expected %.10f, got %.10f (error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, j, expected, actual, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size N (computes NxN * NxN) (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    auto finish = [](int code) {\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return code;\n    };\n\n    size_t N = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on every rank)\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            N = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return finish(0);\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return finish(1);\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Matrix Multiplication Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", N, N);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n        printf(\"MPI ranks: %d\\n\", size);\n    }\n\n    // Each rank owns a contiguous block of rows of A and C. B is replicated.\n    const RowPartition part = partitionRows(N, rank, size);\n    std::vector<double> A(part.numRows * N);\n    std::vector<double> B(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> C(part.numRows * N);\n\n    // Initialize matrices (generated locally; no communication required)\n    if (root) printf(\"Initializing matrices...\\n\");\n    initMatrixRows(A, N, part.firstRow, part.numRows);\n    initMatrixRows(B, N, 0, N);\n\n    // Perform distributed matrix multiplication\n    if (root) printf(\"Computing matrix multiplication...\\n\");\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    const double t0 = MPI_Wtime();\n\n    matrixMultiplyRows(A.data(), B.data(), C.data(), part.numRows, N);\n\n    const double localSec = MPI_Wtime() - t0;\n\n    // The slowest rank determines the wall-clock time of the parallel run\n    double maxSec = 0.0;\n    MPI_Reduce(&localSec, &maxSec, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n    if (root) {\n        const auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(\n            std::chrono::duration<double>(maxSec));\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", static_cast<long>(duration.count()));\n\n        // Calculate GFLOPS\n        double gflops = (2.0 * N * N * N) / maxSec / 1e9;\n        printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    }\n\n    // Gather the full result on rank 0 only when it is needed for output or validation\n    const bool needFull = printResults || validate;\n    std::vector<double> fullC;\n    if (needFull) {\n        if (root) fullC.resize(N * N);\n\n        // Row-typed gather: counts and displacements are in rows, avoiding int overflow\n        MPI_Datatype rowType;\n        MPI_Type_contiguous(static_cast<int>(N), MPI_DOUBLE, &rowType);\n        MPI_Type_commit(&rowType);\n\n        std::vector<int> counts(size), displs(size);\n        for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n            const RowPartition p = partitionRows(N, r, size);\n            counts[r] = static_cast<int>(p.numRows);\n            displs[r] = static_cast<int>(p.firstRow);\n        }\n\n        MPI_Gatherv(C.data(), static_cast<int>(part.numRows), rowType,\n                    fullC.data(), counts.data(), displs.data(), rowType, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n        MPI_Type_free(&rowType);\n    }\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults && root) {\n        print_results(fullC, \"MatrixC\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    int valid = 1;\n    if (validate) {\n        if (root) {\n            printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n            valid = validateResult(fullC, N) ? 1 : 0;\n            printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", valid ? \"PASSED\" : \"FAILED\");\n        }\n        // Broadcast so every rank exits with the same status\n        MPI_Bcast(&valid, 1, MPI_INT, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        return finish(valid ? 0 : 1);\n    }\n\n    return finish(0);\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/matmul/matmul.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/matmul/matmul.cpp","time":{"start":1793033985706,"end":1793033985768}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_1792736bc001zns3o24tla8pdZ","sessionID":"ses_e86d9c73dffeXEMyYZnYJcH9C9","messageID":"msg_179272d35001IxBd3phwig3Fa7"}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793034216286,"sessionID":"ses_e86d9c73dffeXEMyYZnYJcH9C9","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"edit","callID":"toolu_01KeCHVFH5JpfsyWZihoJQ5b","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/matmul/matmul.cpp","oldString":"// For every C(i,j) the products are accumulated in ascending k order starting\n// from 0.0, which is the same summation order as the naive triple loop.\nvoid matrixMultiplyRows(const double* A, const double* B, double* C, const size_t numRows, const size_t N) {\n    constexpr size_t KB = 64;   // k-block: B panel of KB x JB doubles stays in L2\n    constexpr size_t JB = 256;  // j-block: C row segment stays in L1\n\n    std::fill(C, C + numRows * N, 0.0);\n\n    for (size_t jj = 0; jj < N; jj += JB) {\n        const size_t jEnd = std::min(jj + JB, N);\n        for (size_t kk = 0; kk < N; kk += KB) {\n            const size_t kEnd = std::min(kk + KB, N);\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < numRows; ++i) {\n                double* c = C + i * N;\n                const double* a = A + i * N;\n                for (size_t k = kk; k < kEnd; ++k) {\n                    const double aik = a[k];\n                    const double* b = B + k * N;\n                    for (size_t j = jj; j < jEnd; ++j) {\n                        c[j] += aik * b[j];\n                    }","newString":"// For every C(i,j) the products are accumulated in ascending k order starting\n// from 0.0, which is the same summation order as the naive triple loop. The\n// accumulation uses an explicit fused multiply-add so that the rounding matches\n// the original kernel's compiled behavior bit-for-bit.\nvoid matrixMultiplyRows(const double* A, const double* B, double* C, const size_t numRows, const size_t N) {\n    constexpr size_t KB = 64;   // k-block: B panel of KB x JB doubles stays in L2\n    constexpr size_t JB = 256;  // j-block: C row segment stays in L1\n\n    std::fill(C, C + numRows * N, 0.0);\n\n    for (size_t jj = 0; jj < N; jj += JB) {\n        const size_t jEnd = std::min(jj + JB, N);\n        for (size_t kk = 0; kk < N; kk += KB) {\n            const size_t kEnd = std::min(kk + KB, N);\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < numRows; ++i) {\n                double* c = C + i * N;\n                const double* a = A + i * N;\n                for (size_t k = kk; k < kEnd; ++k) {\n                    const double aik = a[k];\n                    const double* b = B + k * N;\n                    for (size_t j = jj; j < jEnd; ++j) {\n                        c[j] = std::fma(aik, b[j], c[j]);\n                    }"},"output":"Edit applied successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"diff":"Index: /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/matmul/matmul.cpp\n===================================================================\n--- /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/matmul/matmul.cpp\n+++ /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/matmul/matmul.cpp\n@@ -42,9 +42,11 @@\n \n // Local block multiply: C (numRows x N) = A (numRows x N) * B (N x N).\n // Cache-blocked i-k-j loop order with a contiguous, vectorizable inner loop.\n // For every C(i,j) the products are accumulated in ascending k order starting\n-// from 0.0, which is the same summation order as the naive triple loop.\n+// from 0.0, which is the same summation order as the naive triple loop. I'm considering whether GCC could be auto-vectorizing the reduction loop across k even without fast-math flags, which would change the summation order and explain the fma-related discrepancy, but on x86 that's generally not permitted without associative-math enabled -- so I'm wondering if unrolling is causing a subtly different accumulation order instead.\n\nRather than reasoning further, I think it's faster to just write a minimal test program with the same inputs and compare both summation orders directly, or disassemble the reference's matrix multiply loop to see exactly how it accumulates.\n\n","time":{"start":1793034358030,"end":1793034366156},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793034379148,"sessionID":"ses_e86d9c73dffeXEMyYZnYJcH9C9","part":{"id":"prt_1792d3d7e001Hnjw3ocqNh54CR","messageID":"msg_1792d341e0012JYkPBfRabnL9q","sessionID":"ses_e86d9c73dffeXEMyYZnYJcH9C9","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm realizing GCC vectorized the reduction across k into two lanes (even/odd), computing paired products and then summing the partials together, which explains the instruction ordering I'm seeing.\n\nSo the vector body uses separate multiply and add instructions while the scalar tail uses a fused multiply-add — meaning the reference output's rounding is inherently inconsistent, since fp-contract behavior differs between the vectorized and tail paths. Exactly reproducing that mixed behavior is compiler-artifact-dependent and probably not worth chasing bit-for-bit; I think accepting small last-bit differences with tolerance-based validation is the pragmatic choice, since my own FMA-everywhere kernel can't match that hybrid pattern, though my strict non-FMA build does match the strict sequential sum case exactly.\n\nI'm leaning toward strict IEEE semantics as the defensible choice — deterministic and matching the original's source-level sum without fusion — and I'd enforce it with `-ffp-contract=off` in CMake. There's a tradeoff though: non-FMA costs some theoretical throughput, but the kernel is likely memory/latency bound anyway, so I want to actually benchmark both FMA and non-FMA versions at a larger size before committing.\n\n","time":{"start":1793034370430,"end":1793034379093},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793034379149,"sessionID":"ses_e86d9c73dffeXEMyYZnYJcH9C9","part":{"id":"prt_1792d5f58001mZw4L79zF17ub7","messageID":"msg_1792d341e0012JYkPBfRabnL9q","sessionID":"ses_e86d9c73dffeXEMyYZnYJcH9C9","type":"text","text":"The reference's inner loop is compiled differently from the source: GCC vectorizes the k-reduction with unfused multiplies and adds in the vector body and fuses only the scalar tail. So the original's `-r` bits depend on the optimizer's contraction choices, and no FMA-based kernel can reproduce them exactly. The one well-defined reference is strict IEEE semantics: `-ffp-contract=off` gives the same hash as the source's `sum += a*b`. My non-FMA kernel matched that exactly earlier.\n\nI'll switch to the plain `c[j] += aik * b[j]` form and set `-ffp-contract=off` for this target, so results are deterministic and match the source's semantics.
